title: Invented betting advert
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y10 lesson 3 (Invented betting advert (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 3: Gambling and risk: why it harms. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: What counts as gambling?
points: Some game features feel similar: loot boxes

model.title: A game: pay £1, 1 in 6 chance to win £5 (you keep the prize, not your £1). Expected result per go?

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: You lose about 17p each go on average

passage.title: LUCKYSPIN (invented for this lesson)
paras: Join tonight and get a £20 FREE BET! Risk-free!
Thousands win every day. Could you be next? Offer ends at midnight!
Download now and spin in seconds.
Small print: 18+. Free bet must be wagered 30 times before winnings can be withdrawn. Terms apply.

questions.q: Name three persuasion techniques in the advert.
questions.a: Any three: 'free bet' and 'risk-free' (a gift that is not free); time pressure ('ends at midnight'); suggesting winning is common ('thousands win'); making it quick and easy ('spin in seconds').

questions.q: What does the advert hide or play down?
questions.a: The house edge (players lose on average); the 30x wagering condition in the small print; the risk of addiction and debt.

questions.q: Using the lesson's game (pay £1, 1 in 6 chance of £5), how much would you expect to lose in 60 goes?
questions.a: Expected loss about 17p a go, so about £10 in 60 goes (60 x £1 = £60 paid; 10 expected wins x £5 = £50).

keywords.def: risking money on an uncertain result to win more
the built-in advantage that makes the operator win over time
a paid random reward in a video game

questions.q: Pay £2 for a 1 in 10 chance of £15 (prize only). Expected loss per go?
Core: Advert analysis (pupil PDF): identify three persuasion techniques in an invented betting advert and what it hides.
questions.a: Free bets, celebrity, 'win big'; hides losses and risks.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain whether loot boxes are like gambling. Start: 'Loot boxes are similar because...'
questions.a: Similar: pay for a random reward; can encourage repeated spending; Muslims should avoid chance-based paid rewards.

questions.q: Stretch: Where can someone get help with gambling harm?
questions.a: Parents, GP, the National Gambling Helpline (GamCare).

questions.q: Why do gambling operators make profit overall?
options: The odds give them an edge
questions.a: B) The odds give them an edge. The house edge means players lose on average over time.

questions.q: Maysir means... A) charity B) gambling, forbidden in Islam C) trade
Big question: why do companies make billions if adverts show winners?
questions.a: Most people lose over time because of the house edge.
